scope: Bounded API batch result transport; exact external result values/order and existing data/meta envelope

dependency.ownership: Operations agent; copied for focused integration only, excluded from this commit.

protocol.commands_executed_in: One canonical database transaction; no automatic mutation or read retry
protocol.result_handling: Original immutable UTF-8 JSON bytes are streamed; only array punctuation is emitted by API. Exact result JSON is never parsed or reconstructed.
protocol.integrity: Receipt, result ordinal, chunk index, fixed lengths, canonical base64, per-chunk SHA256 and incremental whole-result SHA256; missing or corrupt output never closes a success envelope.

migrated.scope: Real migrated local SQL plus actual API and production chunk consumer, synthetic PostgREST/Auth/Storage transport. Not real PostgREST resource qualification.

verification.independent_review: Source-only framing/cancellation/base64/hash/paging review found no material blocker; reviewer did not rerun tests.

coverage: Existing100-command boundary preserves all results and one mutation call.
Exact Arabic UTF-8 split across fixed chunks, escaped text, null/boolean/numeric values and raw numeric lexical representation.
Malformed manifest, invalid UTF-8/JSON, response frame overflow, wrong receipt/index/order/length/hash and repeated final chunk reject.
Caller and consumer cancellation retain API admission until active or late noncooperative fetch/source settles.
No chunk prefetch before downstream demand or while consumer paused.
Known mutation errors retain existing mapping; read-time SQL57014 and network ambiguity are nonretryable and never resubmit committed commands.
Existing migrated atomicity/revision/idempotency/access checks continue through new manifest/chunk adapters.
qualification_limits: SQL remains responsible for immutable canonical valid JSON bytes, current authority, retention and legacy compatibility.
The separate normalized SQL migration, actual PostgREST128MiB10/100-result proof and historical aggregate normalization/cutover must be qualified before deployment.
Existing admission is per API handler; local tests are not native peak-memory, NGINX backpressure, network disconnect or cluster-wide proof.
No provider call, production mutation, new billing/model quota or deployment occurred.
